title: The Donkey Who Played Watchdog
text:
In the city of Varanasi lived a washerman who kept a donkey to carry his loads and a dog to guard his house. One night, after a long day, he was sleeping soundly when a thief crept into the yard.

The donkey saw the thief and nudged the dog. Bark, he said, that is your job. The dog refused. Our master has neglected me, he complained. He feeds me badly and takes me for granted. Let him lose something, and then he will remember what I am worth.

The donkey was outraged. A servant, he said, should not bargain in an emergency. If the dog would not do his duty, the donkey would do it for him. He lifted his head and brayed as loudly as he could.

The washerman woke with a start, furious at being disturbed. He saw no thief, only his donkey making a racket in the middle of the night. He picked up a stick and beat the donkey hard, then went back to sleep.
lesson: Each role on a team exists for a reason. Doing another person's job out of indignation, without the means to do it well, can bring trouble on you instead of solving the problem.
people: A washerman, his donkey, his dog, a thief
